requirement_text.REQ-006: Domain vocabulary decision: content_ba_guide.md §4's domain vocabulary terms — Event, Chapter, Talk, Speaker, CFP, Agenda, Check-in, Going, Watching — STAY IN ENGLISH VERBATIM in the Kazakh copy, exactly as they already do in the Russian, Uzbek, and English copy. These are established cross-locale product/brand terms shared across all AI Qadam surfaces regardless of body-copy language. Surrounding sentence structure, headings, and connecting prose around these terms are still fully translated into Kazakh — only the specific vocabulary tokens listed above remain untranslated.

task.description:
REVIEWER FAILed REQ-006 (rework iteration 1 of 3). BLOCKING issue: the domain-vocabulary rule was misapplied. The requirement text says these terms stay English 'exactly as they already do in the Russian... copy' — but messages/ru.json actually translates Event/Chapter/Talk natively into Russian (событие/события for 'event', чаптер/чаптеры for 'chapter', доклад for 'talk'); only CFP genuinely appears verbatim in English in ru.json. Fix by translating the wrongly-English-left instances into native Kazakh, matching what ru.json's corresponding key actually does — Kazakh equivalents for событие/события ('іс-шара'/'іс-шаралар' or similar — use your own judgment for natural, idiomatic Kazakh, this is not prescribed), чаптер/чаптеры (a Kazakh transliteration or native equivalent, matching how the Russian keeps 'чаптер' as an established loanword — Kazakh commonly does the same, 'чаптер' is likely fine as a Kazakh loanword too, but verify against how you'd naturally write it), доклад ('баяндама' or similar). Only CFP stays English-verbatim per this requirement's decision, since that's the one term ru.json itself keeps in English.

Specific keys REVIEWER flagged: Nav.events, Nav.chapters, Hero.ctaPrimary, Band.lede, Doors.door1Body, Doors.door2Link, Events.eyebrow, Streams.stream1Title, Partners.partner1Desc, MapSection.ctaLaunchChapter, MapSection.nodeAlmatySub, Team.team5Role. Also fix the MINOR issue: Footer.licenseCode/licenseContent/licenseBrand leave Russian plain nouns 'КОД'/'КОНТЕНТ'/'БРЕНД' untranslated — translate these into Kazakh (they are not domain-vocabulary terms or names), keeping the trailing license values (MIT, CC BY 4.0, AI QADAM BUP) verbatim.

After fixing the flagged keys, do a full re-scan of messages/kk.json for any other instance of the same pattern (an English word substituted for a Russian word that ru.json actually translates) that REVIEWER's spot-check may not have caught — don't assume the flagged list is exhaustive.
acceptance_criteria: All 12 flagged keys (Nav.events, Nav.chapters, Hero.ctaPrimary, Band.lede, Doors.door1Body, Doors.door2Link, Events.eyebrow, Streams.stream1Title, Partners.partner1Desc, MapSection.ctaLaunchChapter, MapSection.nodeAlmatySub, Team.team5Role) now hold natural Kazakh translations of the corresponding ru.json meaning, with only CFP (where it occurs) staying English-verbatim
Footer.licenseCode/licenseContent/licenseBrand translated into Kazakh, license values (MIT, CC BY 4.0, AI QADAM BUP) kept verbatim
A full re-scan performed for the same pattern elsewhere in the file, any additional instances fixed and reported
messages/kk.json remains valid JSON with the same 177-key structure
No new Cyrillic-Russian-vs-Kazakh regressions introduced (spot-check a few unrelated keys to confirm they weren't accidentally touched)

gate_history.summary: Domain-vocabulary rule misapplied: Event/Chapter/Talk left in literal English at 12 keys where ru.json actually translates these words natively into Russian; only CFP is a genuine verbatim-English term in ru.json. Also Footer license-line labels left untranslated.
